prompt: A skip list promotes each node with independent coin flips. Why do higher levels normally contain fewer nodes?

options.text: Insertion deletes keys from the lower levels.
options.explanation: Every key remains on the bottom level.

options.text: Reaching a higher level requires succeeding at every promotion below it.
options.explanation: Correct. Each additional independent promotion filters the population again.

options.text: The structure sorts by tower height instead of key.
options.explanation: Each level remains ordered by key.

options.text: Each level is forced to contain exactly half the keys.
options.explanation: Promotion determines expected proportions, not exact quotas.

workedExample: Every node starts at the bottom. Only promoted nodes reach the next level, and only promoted members of that smaller group reach the next. Independent promotion makes higher lanes progressively sparser on average; any particular run can differ.
